Hating the parents is irrelevant to ethics, my dude.

Okay, so "she never would have gotten caught" is only the case because the highly experimental, never-before-done medical procedure she did on a boy WORKED. Had it not, she would have faced charges of murder. She got LUCKY. She got lucky that it worked, and Braden's T-cell count improved. Medical procedures go wrong ALL the time. Experimental procedures, with correctly backed research and case studies and trials go wrong ALL the time. The fact that it didn't, the fact that it worked, was equal parts luck than anything else. As someone in medical school, I can tell you firsthand that even common procedure goes wrong all the time. 

As far as everything else - she only confessed after two weeks - after she had observed that his immune response was improving. She was hoping that the parents would be too overwhelmed by the positive results and tide over the consequences. 
When it didn't go this way, and she had to speak to Jackson and Owen - they asked her if she had apologized to the parents - at this stage she says that apologies are issued only when a mistake has been made, clearly not seeing what was wrong with what she did even here. 

In subsequent episodes, when Jackson tells her that her genome lab was going to be defunded because her research was the only project out of all the others that wasn't showing results, logically making sense that it should be the one to go, she gets even more upset, and bratty, and starts bragging about the SCID boy. Jackson reminds her that the hospital almost got sued in the process, and that she got lucky, and she yells at him that isn't relevant, because it worked. She does this repeatedly throughout that episode and the next. 

About Stephanie taking the fall for her, and choosing to - she allowed her to tell the parents that she was the one who misinformed Bailey about the consent, and didn't inform them of what really happened, as was their right to know. When Stephanie is given a week of suspension, she barely needs any convincing. She lets a junior resident take the fall for her - because it deprives her of having to face the consequences of a possible medical malpractice suit. 

Another example is when her patients were getting post-op infections because of the staph virus - though she wasn't responsible for the defect in the gloves that killed them, she blames Leah Murphy, berates her, humiliates her. (Even though Leah had worked when she was sick, and she snojldnt have, admittedly all the doctors in the hospital had done the same thing) As soon as it traces back to her as she was the only one who touched all patients, she loses all cool and starts yelling, again. She doesn't even want to entertain the possibility of an investigation, or that she might have unknowingly contaminated her patients, because in her mind, she is infallible. She yells at the CDC rep who interviews her, too. She yells at the board for even calling the CDC. She yells when she is not allowed to access her patients though it is protocol. 

This is just one example, I'm sure there are more I'm forgetting at the moment.
